spatial_claims.claim: G lies on ray AB from A, with AG = DE
H lies on ray AC from A, with AH = DF
Angle GAH = Angle BAC because G is on ray AB and H is on ray AC (rays coincide)
Triangles ABC and AGC have bases AB and AG on the same straight line (A, G, B collinear) with common vertex C
Triangles AGH and AGC have bases AH and AC on the same straight line (A, H, C collinear) with common vertex G
Height from C to line AB is the same for triangles ABC and AGC; height from G to line AC is the same for triangles AGH and AGC

configuration_map: Triangle ABC given with angle BAC. Triangle DEF given separately with angle EDF = angle BAC. Point G constructed on ray AB from A with AG = DE, so A, G, B are collinear (G between A and B, or at B, or beyond B depending on magnitudes). Point H constructed on ray AC from A with AH = DF, so A, H, C are collinear (similarly flexible). Triangle AGH is congruent to triangle DEF by SAS (1.4). Triangle AGC serves as the key intermediary: it shares vertex C with triangle ABC (enabling the first 6.1 application via common height from C to line AB) and shares vertex G with triangle AGH (enabling the second 6.1 application via common height from G to line AC). All constructions lie in the plane of triangle ABC.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. G on ray AB and H on ray AC ensure valid collinearity for both applications of 6.1 (same-height triangle pairs). The angle equality angle GAH = angle BAC follows directly from G and H lying on the respective rays. No angle decompositions, no inside/outside claims, and no betweenness issues arise. The proof uses only proportional reasoning (5.7, 5.11, 5.9) after establishing the geometric configuration, with no conflicting spatial requirements.
